chapters.html:
There was a naked man in his freezer.

Personally, words Mydei had never thought he’d say, but he supposed there was a first time for everything.

He’d really just had been trying to close up shop when he’d found the man passed out in the back rooms of his quaint little cafes freezer. He’d quite literally just shooed out his workers, earlier than usual, because they were university students in the middle of exam term and needed all the help they could get.

“I’ll be fine,” he had said in agitation, shaking his head when they had expressed concern for him. “Whats the worst that could possibly happen at 9 pm on a Wednesday?”

This, apparently.

Mydei cursed under his breath. Just his luck. There was a man passed out in his freezer right under the frozen breakfast sausages. This would look terrible if it ever got out. He could see the headlines now. Crazy Kremnoan moves to Okhema just to cook their citizens. He sighed loudly and fairly dramatically at the thought. Everyone was going to think he was a front for a mob organization now or something.

He sat down on his knees heavily, taking a moment just to look the man over. He mainly did this to check him over for signs of life, but something else managed to take his breath away. 

He was-

He was beautiful.

… Too beautiful, to the point where even attempting to define him in typical common words felt like such an understatement he may as well have not tried at all. He was a Greek statue come to life, carved from marble and chiseled to perfection. As if Mydei could reach out a hand, place it against his cheek, and watch him crumble into nothing. Not a single imperfection laced his skin, and that in of itself was its own source of wrongness. As if someone had tried to parody humanity with only the most divine images to copy from.

It was, for lack of better words, fake. The person in front of him, passed out in his freezer, felt fake, so far removed from even the concept of flaws as he was. 

But by the titans, he was divine. 

And bleeding. He was also bleeding. Badly. That was probably what Mydei should've been focusing on.

A quick glance downward, while avoiding the very large elephant in the room, because he was respectful and the man was bleeding out, was all he really needed. There was no way the man wasn’t dead. The wounds deep in his torso looked like something a bear or other particularly large feral animal would create, cut deep and jagged into his guts. He should’ve been one step into heaven's gates by now. Yet, the blood remained sitting inside the wounds, defying any physics they were meant to follow.

Then again, the blood was gold, so maybe there were bigger problems here. Mydei didn’t even know how that was possible, could you get your blood to change colour through cosmetic surgery or something? That sounded horrific.

Right, dying man. Mydei thought he may have been in shock, with how quickly his mind seemed to flutter.

Even with the confidence that the person in front of him was dead, that someone had likely planted his body here to frame Mydei, and that he would be spending a lot of time trying to explain this to his parents, he still leaned down to check the man’s pulse before anything else. On the slight, off chance, that he was alive.

Only to flinch back when a hand reached out and curled around his wrist, mere moments before he could press his hand to his neck.

Mydei hissed, the feeling of burning wringing through his body’s nerves as that wrist tightened.

His freezer. His freezer was … warm?

Why was his freezer warm?

He couldn’t do anything but watch as the man’s eyes snapped open and he lurched forward, darting from the cart of butter in front of him, to the dough tray, before finally sliding over to meet Mydei’s eyes.

Intense. Golden eyes held his own with a fervor, staring straight through him and seeing something even Mydei couldn’t quite grasp. A gasp caught in his throat, and despite how hard he tried, he couldn’t seem to let it escape. Something deep within him urged him to recoil away, but the grip of his wrist was firm and unyielding.

The man tilted his head, ever so slightly, leaning in close. Oh, there was a hint of blue there, in his eyes. Mydei couldn’t help but latch on to that, feeling himself drawn to the way those blonde lashes seemed to flutter gently, brushing against his cheeks as he stared up at Mydei, looking at him like he was the only man in the world.

They were studying him, those eyes. Despite having woken up in what was likely a strange place, with a strange man standing over him, not once had his eyes felt hazy or lost. They held a sharpness that was almost unnerving, as if he hadn’t waited even a second before he began observing.

He just stared at him, and Mydei could not look away. For what felt like hours but must have only been a few minutes at best, they watched each other. Where had he seen those eyes before? He knew he had, but where exactly escaped his grasp. He couldn’t remember for the life of him.

Then, like the rising of the sun, the man smiled, the wariness and cold of his eyes replaced with a light of bliss. It was such a sudden switch that Mydei swore he imagined it.

“Found you,” he murmured, his voice a gentle cascade on his ears, like the pleasing notes of a choir. Then, as he leaned forward, he collapsed into his arms fully. Mydei choked, that heat almost overwhelming him as a man who practically shared his own impressive height and stature threw his entire body weight onto him. Mydei felt like an outside observer in his own body as he watched the very beautiful, still very much naked man he’d found in his freezer nuzzle up against his chest.

He went under just as quickly as he came up, bright gold eyes flickering closed as he stared up at Mydei, a content sigh leaving his lips.

And Mydei? He sat there, completely bewildered, and wondered why he was the only one who managed to wind up in situations like this. Then, after taking a couple moments to lock in, heaved the man up into his arms, carried him up into the one bedroom apartment he’d converted into a living space right above his bakery, and set him down.

After finding a roll of gauze in the back of the closet, he got to work on disinfecting the wounds. By the time he was done, the sun had risen into the sky come dawn, and for the first time in Mydei’s life, it felt less like a blessing and more like a warning.

Mydei sighed, threw his now odd coloured bloody clothes in the washer, decided to take the other man to a doctor in the morning, and closed the shop for the day. Then he took the longest nap of his entire life.

── ⟢ ・⸝⸝

By the time he’d woken up, the sun had drifted down into the midline, the start of a new cycle approaching.

He would’ve, could’ve, should’ve probably just let himself sleep through the night and woken up the next morning, but something dragged him back into consciousness. Probably the half dead man he’d put to bed last night.

Mydei blinked his eyes open, and promptly screamed.

“Oh my god,” he said, hand clutched to his chest. “How are you moving?”

The man, practically on top of Mydei with how close he was to his face, tilted his head sideways as blue eyes bore into his soul. Then he smiled, leaning his head forward to nuzzle into the crook of his neck.

“Okay,” Mydei said, staring up at the ceiling. Then, with some effort, he pulled his hands up and tried to push the man away. “Well, good to know you didn’t die. Is there something different about you? I swear your eyes were gold, before.

No response. Mydei sighed, then pushed against harder.

He may as well have been shoving against a solid brick wall. Maybe he was just tired, but it seemed impossible to get the man off of him. Mydei sighed, collapsing backwards onto his bed.

“We have to get you some clothes,” Mydei said quietly, keeping his eyes tilted away in respect. “Then take you to a hospital. Maybe get you a breakfast wrap. How hard could that be?”

── ⟢ ・⸝⸝

Very hard, clearly. 

The strange man insisted on clinging onto him every step of the way, an added 190 pounds lugging behind him, and no matter how many times Mydei shoved him off, he came back stronger and clingier somehow.

He did manage to get some sweats on him, so at least he likely wouldn’t feel as uncomfortable anymore.

Mydei stared plainly at the breakfast wrap in process in front of him, dragging some eggs off the stove. “Do you have any preferences? Allergies I should know about?”

Silence, only a far too knowing stare boring into his back.

“Okay, you’re getting eggs and sausage.” Mydei said, pulling out some chipotle sauce. “After you eat this, we’ll leave for the clinic. It’s fairly far, and I don’t have a car, so we’ll have to take a shortcut through the forest.”

“Leave?” he asked. It was the first word he had said since Mydei had woken up, and it caused his eyes to widen. The tilt was off key and wonky, like the word hadn’t come out right from the throat. 

“Yes,” Mydei said, hoping his own voice came off as comforting and not deeply unsettled. “I’ll take you to get your wounds checked out.”

He blinked. Mydei felt his brows furrow. He wasn’t confused about what he was saying, right? Mydei felt like he was being fairly clear, all things considered.

“You,” he pointed. The man stared at his finger. “Me,” he pulled it back to himself, then pointed towards the door. “Doctor. Out.”

The reaction was instantaneous. He shook his head, whipping it back and forth desperately.

“No,” he panted, a hand against his chest. “No, don’t leave.”

“I’m not-“ Mydei said, then closed his eyes and took a deep breath. “We’d leave together. I’m not sending you out on your own.”

“No,” he insisted, over and over again. The tone and voice pressed on Mydei’s ears, over and over again. It was too much, like his agony was spreading onto Mydei in waves. It hit in ways that made him nauseous, like he’d do anything to make it stop.

“Okay!” Mydei shook his head, holding his hands up in a stop motion. “Fine, fine. I’ll check your wounds first, but if they’re infected or worsening, we have to.”

That seemed to be enough for him, as his words cut off sharply, silence filling the cafe’s kitchen instead.

Mydei finished the wrap, gently pushing it over towards the man, who took it like he wasn’t quite sure what to do with it. He watched Mydei keenly, eyes wide, following his movements with his own. He ate methodically, like he was barely aware of his own actions. Yet, his eyes seemed to almost shine. He scarfed it down faster than Mydei could blink.

Mydei took that as a positive. He was also slightly concerned, he hadn’t even seen the guy chew.

“Is it … alright?” Mydei asked curiously, raising an eyebrow as he finished his own food, much slower.

A stiff nod, hands coming up to link at the digits.

Mydei blinked, then raised an eyebrow. “Would you like another one?”

Another nod, more eager. Mydei felt a small smile work its way onto his face as he got up, pulling out the ingredients once more.

“So, now that you’ve got some food into your stomach, mind telling me your name?” Mydei asked, turning the stove back on.

“Name,” he murmured, somewhere behind Mydei. The sound of shuffling, slowly increasing in volume. “my name, my name is-“

Mydei turned around just in time to watch him open his mouth. However, nothing seemed to come out. His voice was fractured like static, and whatever was said was incomprehensible to Mydei’s ears. The sounds were filled with what had to have been a cacophony of violence and dread. Whatever it was, it dug its way into his mind like a vicious virus.

Blood trickled down Mydei’s ear, running down his neck. He reached a hand up, feeling the warmth in his fingertip. He thinks time might have stopped.

He was rotting. He was crying, he thought, or maybe he was.

Mydei looked up, and the walls stopped pulsing around him, his headache fading away.

“Well,” Mydei said after a moment, pulling his hand back down. “I don’t believe that was english, actually.”

The other man looked deeply distraught at this, his brows furrowing. He opened his mouth, debated for a moment, then clicked it close.

“You’re bleeding,” he said instead, rising from his seat with a small napkin. Mydei took it from him with a small thank you, his hands shaking just barely under the lights.

He sat back down again, roughly, as Mydei patched up his own wound. When he was done, he finished making the wrap, shooing his apologies off.

“That’s never happened before, but it's not like you made my ears bleed, so stop apologizing,” Mydei said with a scoff, taking his dirty plate and leaving it in the fridge.

He held the wrap in his hands, turning to look at Mydei’s retreating figure with an odd look in his eyes.

“Thank you,” he said after a moment of silence. His voice was like honey on bread, sickingly smooth. “For making me this. I’ve been so hungry for so long.”

Mydei blinked. Swallowed roughly. The blood was soaking through the napkin. He should replace it.

“You’re welcome,” he said cautiously. “Take your time, I’ll get the first aid kit and we can recheck your wounds.”

The man nodded, turning back to his food, and Mydei left him there, but not without one final glance. He ate like a ravenous dog, biting and tearing at the food as if it would disappear before his eyes. Mydei watched, enraptured, before he urged himself to turn away.

── ⟢ ・⸝⸝

“Phainon,” he’d said, lying in bed while Mydei pulled out the wrappings.

“What?” Mydei asked, eyes flickering upwards. “Is that your name?”

Silence, a tongue licking at his lips, a sharp canine glinting in the lamplight.

“Yes,” he said. “My name is … Phainon.”

Mydei felt his eyebrows crease. He looked up, stared at him for a moment.

“Are you sure?” Mydei asked.

Phainon blinked. “I would certainly hope so, yes.”

“Huh,” Mydei said, looking back down.”…it’s a nice name. Thank you for telling me.”

“Anything,” Phainon breathed. Mydei did not deign that with a response.

“Oh,” he said instead, as the bandages fell.

His chest, torso, his entire abdomen had been completely mended. If not the faint lines that showed something had been sealed up, Mydei thought he may not have noticed anything at all. Unbidden, his hand reached out, faintly tracing the thin lines. It left a small, odd coloured stain of blood on his fingertip.

“It’s good, right? Mydei?” Phainon asked, and Mydei tore his eyes away from his chest. He was staring down at him, wide eyed, searching longingly for approval.

“I- yes, I suppose it is,” Mydei felt his gaze flicker back down, away from those piercing eyes. “How on earth did they heal in barely a day?” He said under his breath, hands moving to close the first aid kit.

“I’m glad!” Phainon broke through his musings, knocking the bandages away and leaning closer towards Mydei. “That means I don’t have to leave, right?”

“…Do you feel any lingering pain? Any causes for concern?” Mydei asked, his eyes red dressing the longer he stared at Phainon’s eyes. Perhaps it would still be best to take him, just to get out of this damned house for a while.

“Nope!” Phainon chirped, shaking his head. “So we can stay, right?”

“… yes, if you’re feeling fine, we can stay.” Mydei agreed, ignoring the churning in his gut telling him not to do that. Phainon almost seemed to purr at his answer.

“You seem to be feeling better, at the very least,” Mydei said, relief coating his tone. “You’re certain you don’t remember anything at all? No idea how you ended up in my fridge?”

“Mm, nope!” Phainon said again. “All I remember is you, Mydei.”

“That’s probably not good,” Mydei said. Then, “I’ll put out some calls and talk to the authorities to see if anyone’s heard of you, but with how small Aedes Elysiae is, I wouldn’t hold my breath.”

A smile brightened up Phainon’s face at the words, as if that was what he’d been waiting for. The way the smile stretched against his face made Mydei’s hackles rise, almost instinctively.

“Where else would I go?” He asked curiously, his eyes falling shut. “I’m already home.”

── ⟢ ・⸝⸝

Phainon was not a terrible roommate, all things considered. Also, something deep inside Mydei’s heart clenched whenever he thought about him, which was probably a cause for concern and maybe something to bring up during his next doctors appointment.

Sure, Phainon didn’t know how most modern appliances worked, he was incapable of using the Uber app, and he had an odd habit of leaving animal carcasses around the edges of Kremnos Cafe, but really, who was he to discourage hobbies. Maybe he was just big on Taxidermy.

His presence was enough to keep all of his former employees away, and had very few people dining in. The only one who really stayed was Castorice, who didn’t mind the odd smelling odor behind the dumpster and found the odd aura of death that hung over the cafe oddly comforting, her worlds, not his.

And also Cipher, who just didn’t really care.

”I think I’m in love with Phainon,” he told her one day, while he was kneading some dough for a loaf of bread.

Cipher sputtered, looking over from where she was drizzling chocolate over some croissants. “The serial killer? Really? You’re a pretty guy, Mydei, you can do better.”

“He’s not a serial killer,” Mydei sighed, his voice tired. “Just because rude customers disappear when he walks off to have a chat with them doesn't mean he kills them.”

“He’s definitely doing something,” Cipher said. “Surely you’ve noticed there’s very clearly something wrong with him. You literally live with him. Yesterday I watched him eat that steak you brought home raw. Not even rare, he ate that shit straight from the packaging.

“Of course I’ve noticed,” Mydei humphed, pressing the dough into a ball and slicing into it. “But he’s still recovering, I’m not going to judge him for his … occasional oddities.”

Then, “that’s where that steak went? Why do I bother seasoning it for him?”

“I think he may be eating people,” Castorice said politely from where she was standing at the register.

“Thank you!” Cipher said. “He’s totally eating people.”

“He’s not eating people,” Mydei sighed. Then he put a hand to his head. He really hoped Phainon wasn’t eating people. That scandal would be impossible to live down.

Aside from that, he was pretty much all Mydei could ask for in a living partner.

He cleaned up after himself, sat with Mydei while he filed his taxes, and even helped with cooking sometimes, although more often than not Mydei would wish he hadn’t.

At some point, he’d become so oddly used to the presence at his side it felt odd to be without it. He’d never really looked for a partner, or even really been all too interested in the idea, so having someone who was always around and available to talk to felt equal parts overwhelming and also fairly nice.

Nobody came looking for Phainon, and so he stayed with Mydei, worming his way into his life like he’d always belonged there.

He got better, as well. His movements were more natural, his gait stronger. His body had filled out when not visibly malnourished. He was still just as ravenous, however. Mydei was certain he could put out a thirteen course meal and Phainon would still ask for dessert afterwards. He pulled his weight, however, so Mydei couldn’t really complain.

“Wow,” Phainon had said, almost a year since Mydei had found him in his freezer. He sipped on an iced coffee. “You have no hobbies, Mydei. I don’t think I’ve ever seen you leave this place if not to go buy groceries.”

Mydei hummed, stirring his stew. “I like my job. I would like to do it before I have to stop.“

Phainon humphed, a sour look on his face. “Yeah, but nobody can do their job forever day in day out, right?”

Then he paused, blinked. “Why would you have to stop? You love making food.”

Mydei sighed, sipping at his stew and making a face. Too little salt. He reached for the shaker.

“I do, and if it were my choice, I’d never stop.” Mydei explained. “You remember how I told you about my family, and how my father only let me open this business under one condition?”

“Mhm,” Phainon hummed. 

“That condition was getting an arranged marriage,” Mydei explained, taking his food again. He grinned at the taste, moving to find the meat he’d cut up. “I’m to marry someone of my family's desired status once I return home. Whether I continue running this business will depend on many factors.”

He turned around. Phainon was staring at him like Mydei had killed his newborn and then set the pieces on fire.

“You’re leaving me?” Phainon said, eyes wide.

“You make it sound like we’re breaking up,” Mydei dished some stew into the other man’s bowl. He sighed. “Phainon, you and I both know this was never going to last forever. I told you about this before.”

The tension in the air was palpable. Mydei pursed his lips. The stew suddenly felt bloated and heavy, like it was sinking into his stomach and simply sitting there.

“I could marry you,” Phainon said suddenly, citing through the silence. Mydei stilled, his spoon halfway into his bowl. “Then you’d never have to stop!”

“Don’t say things you don’t mean,” Mydei flushed, his shoulders hunching, trying to ignore what those words meant to his heart. Phainon didn’t mean that, didn’t feel that way. He was probably just mourning his personal chef.

“You know you can’t, anyways,” Mydei said. “It’s an arranged marriage. My parents already have someone picked out for me.”

He’d never minded this arrangement before. Of course, that was before Phainon had fallen into his life, strangeness and all.

Phainon stared at him, his eyes narrowed in thought.

“If this is all going to end, why don’t we go over into the forest today? Isn’t that where your cottage is, anyway?” Phainon finally said, a small smile playing on his lips. “You’ve never even shown me your home. Won’t you do this one thing for me, before you go?”

Mydei stilled, his hands no longer stirring. Phainon tilted his head at the mood change.

“I don’t want to go into the forest,” Mydei bit out after a moment, the stew simmering in his plate.

Phainon blinked, then stared at him, his head tilted. “Oh? Whatever for?”

Mydei sighed, drying his hands with a towel. Finally, he said, “you’re going to laugh at me, or think I’m crazy, or both.”

Phainon stared at him, a soft smile playing on his lips. “I highly doubt that.”

Mydei shook his head, a grimace falling onto his face. Then, under his breath, he mumbled. “There’s monsters in the woods.”

“Oh,” Phainon said, then he nodded. “Okay.”

Mydei felt his lips pursed, eyes narrowing. “I’m serious.”

“I know.”

Skepticism laced Mydei’s voice. “You don’t think I’m lying?”

“Are you lying?” Phainon asked.

A beat of silence. “No.”

“Then I believe you,” Phainon shrugged, staring at his tea plaintively. “Can we go now? I would like to see your home.”

“Did you not hear what I just said?” Mydei said, slightly agitated. “You know, you don’t have to pretend to believe me. I don’t care.”

“I do believe you!” Phainon insisted, stepping out from behind the counter to round the corner, coming to stand behind Mydei. Solid hands wrapped around his waist, and despite the fact that Mydei had known what was going to happen, he still jolted as a thing of something rang up his spine. He shuddered, and subtly tried to worm his way of his grasp.

If Phainon noticed, he did not mention it. However, he did tighten his arms, just slightly, not enough to truly hold, but enough to have Mydei stilling.

“Mydei,” Phainon murmured, a gust of air from his breath hitting Mydei’s neck. He swallowed harshly, Adam’s apple bidding against his neck. “Mydei, Mydei, won’t you walk me home?”

A shiver, stronger this time. He had never felt more cornered in his life. “Phainon, the monster-“

“Don’t worry,” Phainon said lowly, head dropping into the crook of Mydei’s shoulders. “Don’t worry your little head over some monster. You don’t have to be scared. I’ll protect you.”

“I’m not scared,” Mydei grumbled, even though he was scared, terrified even. The tap was still running, the water filling the sink. It lapped at the edges. Mydei should turn it off.

“Good,” Phainon said, and his breathing picked up, just a bit. His sharp fingernails nicked at Mydei’s waist, hands scrambling.

Then, just as quickly as he’d arrived, Phainon stepped back, a wide smile on his face, and Mydei finally felt like he could breathe again.

“Come on!” Phainon urged, tugging at Mydei’s wrists. “I’ll race you there! Bet I can beat you by a whole ten minutes.”

Then he was gone, door swinging wildly behind him, and Mydeimos, never one to ignore a challenge, ran after him without a second thought.

── ⟢ ・⸝⸝

Mydei hadn’t been lying, there were monsters in the forests, and they followed him. Although, as he ran through the thick greys now, no golden eyes watched him from beyond. 

He’d been here for years now, and still, it remained as unsettling as always, ever since that first night he had arrived, all those years ago.

He’d been barely a child, limbs gangly and heart whole, tottering after his mother through the trees as she told him all about how much she loved the small town of Aedes Elysiae, just a couple hours away from the mainland. 

He had grasped onto the hems of her shirt as she dragged him through the woods towards the property she had owned and loved like it was her own family home. She had adored the open fields and farm lands in a way that came off as almost abnormal, obsessed, as if the very fields were calling out to her.

At some point, those feelings had gone from her to Mydei, he swore. For years, it felt like all he could think of was the open forest that separated Okehema from Aedes Elysiae.

This had been years ago, back when tensions between her and his father had been at their worst, when she would take Mydei and leave for weeks on end. Maybe it had just been a way to cope. After all, where their relationship, their love had almost managed to mend in the later years of Mydei’s childhood, Aedes Elysiae remained in the backdrop of his mind.

The property she’d bought was still there, and it was technically where Mydei was officially living, although he only travelled to it rarely.

The race through the forest had been helpful, since it had been quick. Phainon had gotten there before him, although that was because he’d lept off the path almost instantly, urging Mydei to follow. This, however, was one thing he would never compromise on.
